name: David Kakabadze · Brittany
medium: Watercolour and gouache on paper, forms held by soft, thick, blurred dark outlines, colour bleeding inside them
colour: light paper with soft washes of rose, ochre, violet, cobalt and teal, thick blurred dark-blue outlines
form: Breton houses, windmills, harbours and sailing boats on rippled water, stylised waves as repeated curls, sometimes simplified into flat biomorphic shapes
never: never photographic, never oil-paint texture, never a dark overall ground, never printed text or letters
consent: PUBLIC DOMAIN — the artist died in 1952 (more than 70 years ago); the works are reproductions of his paintings. Portrait: his own self-portrait (public domain).
bio: David Kakabadze (1889–1952), the Georgian avant-garde painter, spent most of the 1920s in Paris and painted the coast of Brittany again and again — houses, mills, harbours and boats in watercolour, held by soft, glowing dark outlines, some of them drifting into pure abstract shapes. This is the light, lyrical side of the painter of the Imereti landscapes.
charterBy: Claude's draft from the 11 watercolours (public domain), 2026-09-29 — split from his oils at the owner's word
bioGe: დავით კაკაბაძე (1889–1952), ქართული ავანგარდის მხატვარი, 1920-იან წლებში პარიზში ცხოვრობდა და ბრეტანის სანაპიროს არაერთხელ ხატავდა — სახლებს, წისქვილებს, ნავსადგურებსა და ნავებს აკვარელით, რბილი, მოკაშკაშე მუქი კონტურებით, ზოგს სუფთა აბსტრაქციამდე მიყვანილს. ეს იმერეთის პეიზაჟების ავტორის მსუბუქი, ლირიკული მხარეა.
